reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows W addition in a TiZrMoW HEA creates Mo-W-rich BCC precipitates and improves dynamic strength and plasticity, but the hypothesis applies this to a different base alloy (HfZrTiTa0.53) without direct evidence that similar precipitates will form, be coherent, or produce the claimed 50% fracture strain increase and energy release enhancement in that system.
premises: W addition to refractory HEAs can induce a dual-phase microstructure with W-rich precipitates
Fine, coherent W-rich precipitates act as obstacles to dislocation motion, increasing dislocation storage and strain hardening
Precipitation strengthening via Orowan looping and dislocation locking raises dynamic yield strength
Enhanced strain hardening and higher dynamic yield strength delay adiabatic shear localization and improve uniform deformation
These microstructural changes lead to improved impact-induced energy release capability
